D01.situation_text: First salary in. The letter said 52,000. The bank says 41,300. HR wants your tax declaration by Friday, and asks if you want to raise your EPF contribution.
D01.why_it_matters: Most people never read a payslip. The gap between CTC and in-hand is the first thing nobody explains.
D01.concept_body: A slice of every salary goes into a retirement fund before you see it. Your employer adds the same amount again. You cannot touch it easily, which is the point.

D01-A.immediate_text: Less tax deducted. About 1,800 more reaches you each month.
D01-A.deferred_text: Payroll emails you about a correction. You spot it. Nobody else on your team did.

D01-B.option_label: Deal with it in March like everyone else
D01-B.immediate_text: Nothing changes. The extra tax keeps going out.
D01-B.deferred_text: March. You scramble to invest 60,000 you do not have, just to claim a refund.

D01-C.immediate_text: Take home drops to 38,700. The money is not gone, it is locked away.
D01-C.deferred_text: Your retirement balance is {retirement_balance}. You have never looked at it before today.

D02.situation_text: You need a place. You have 20,000 saved from before. A studio near office is 18,000. A shared 2BHK is 9,000 for your half. A room 40 minutes out is 6,000.
D02.why_it_matters: Rent is the one decision that repeats 240 times without being re-decided. It sets the ceiling on everything else.

D02-A.immediate_text: Your own place. Rent is 44% of your take home.
D02-A.deferred_text: A full year gone. Rent has eaten one third of every rupee you earned.

D02-B.immediate_text: Less space, more money, a flatmate you barely know.
D02-B.deferred_text: A year in a place you never invite anyone to. Rent took a fifth of your pay.

D02-C.immediate_text: Cheapest option. Three hours a day belong to the road now.
D02-C.deferred_text: You have stopped going out on weekdays. It is too far to come back into town.

D03.situation_text: It is the 24th. Rent went out on the 1st, and what is left has to last until payday, seven days away.
D03.why_it_matters: The first time the money runs out before the month does.

D03-A.immediate_text: Money arrives in ten minutes. So does the question about your spending.
D03-A.deferred_text: Your mother still asks whether you are managing.

D03-B.option_label: Eat at home, cancel everything, ride it out
D03-B.immediate_text: Seven long days. You make it to payday.
D03-B.deferred_text: You know your minimum month is {minimum_month}. You have checked it four times.

D03-C.option_label: Dip into your savings for the week
D03-C.immediate_text: Easy. The savings account goes back to where it was two months ago.
D03-C.deferred_text: Four months in, the savings balance has never crossed 15,000.

D04.situation_text: Your bank can auto-transfer money out on salary day. Or you can save whatever is left at month end.
D04.why_it_matters: Saving what is left produces almost nothing. Order of operations is the whole lesson.
D04.concept_body: Money moved out on the day you are paid gets saved. Money left to save at the end of the month does not. Same salary, different result.

D04-A.immediate_text: Gone before you see it. You adjust within a week.
D04-A.deferred_text: {total_saved} saved without ever feeling it leave.

D04-B.immediate_text: Ambitious. Two of the next four months will be tight.
D04-B.deferred_text: {total_saved} saved, but you borrowed back twice.

D04-C.option_label: Save whatever is left at month end
D04-C.deferred_text: Four months of saving what is left. Total saved: {total_saved}.

D05.situation_text: Your mother's friend sells insurance. Your parents want you to start a policy. 3,000 a month, pays out after 20 years, small life cover included.
D05.why_it_matters: Mixing insurance and investment is the most common first financial mistake in Indian households.
D05.hook_line: Your mother's friend has a policy she wants you to sign.
D05.concept_body: A product that promises both usually does neither well. Cover protects the people who depend on you. Investment grows money. Products that mix them tend to charge for the mixing.

D05-A.immediate_text: Your parents are visibly relieved. The agent shakes your hand.
D05-A.deferred_text: You work out the return. Roughly 4.5% a year, and the life cover is 3 lakhs.

D05-B.immediate_text: Your mother is hurt. Her friend calls twice more.
D05-B.deferred_text: It is still brought up at every family dinner.

D05-C.option_label: Ask what the return and the cover actually are
D05-C.immediate_text: Nobody in the room can answer. Your mother stops talking to you for two days.
D05-C.deferred_text: Your father starts asking the same question about his own policies.

D06.situation_text: Your team eats out daily. 250 a meal, 20 days a month. Saying no now is easier than saying no in month six.
D06.why_it_matters: Small recurring amounts are invisible monthly and enormous annually.

D06-A.immediate_text: You are part of the team from week one.
D06-A.deferred_text: 40,000 spent on lunch. You cannot remember a single meal.

D06-B.immediate_text: In enough conversations to matter, out of enough to save.
D06-B.deferred_text: Roughly half the months you cooked. The other half you did not.

D06-C.immediate_text: You save 5,000 a month and eat alone three days a week.
D06-C.deferred_text: Month eight. You have {total_saved} saved and you are known at work as the tiffin guy.

D07.situation_text: You have 20,000 set aside for emergencies. Savings account, a one year fixed deposit, a liquid fund, or cash at home.
D07.why_it_matters: Emergency money has one job: be available. Return is the second priority, not the first.
D07.hook_line: A close friend needs 25,000 and says three months.
D07.concept_body: Money whose only job is to be there. It is not for returns, so where you keep it is decided by how fast you can reach it, not by what it earns.

D07-A.immediate_text: Available the same day. Earns about 3%.
D07-A.deferred_text: Month nine, a phone screen cracks. The money is there and you barely notice it leave.

D07-B.immediate_text: Earns more. Locked for twelve months.
D07-B.deferred_text: The FD has matured. For twelve months that money was yours and out of reach.

D07-C.immediate_text: Out in a day or two. Earns a little more than savings.
D07-C.deferred_text: The money is spread across three places. You are not sure what the total is.

D07-D.immediate_text: Instantly available. Earns nothing and shrinks with inflation.
D07-D.deferred_text: Some of it went on things you would not have transferred money for.

D08.situation_text: A close friend is starting something and needs 25,000. He says three months. You have 38,000 in total.
D08.why_it_matters: Money lent to friends is usually a gift with extra steps and a damaged friendship attached.

D08-A.immediate_text: He is grateful. You have 13,000 left.
D08-A.deferred_text: Nine months. He has not mentioned it. Neither have you.

D08-B.option_label: Give 10,000 and call it a gift
D08-B.immediate_text: Smaller help, no repayment expected, no resentment either.
D08-B.deferred_text: He never brought it up. You have not either.

D08-C.immediate_text: He says he understands. The call ends early.
D08-C.deferred_text: He found the money elsewhere. Your conversations are shorter now.

D09.situation_text: Your company covers you for 3 lakhs. HR offers 5 lakhs more for 450 a month. Nobody in your family has been seriously ill.
D09.why_it_matters: Health cover is bought when you do not need it or not at all.
D09.hook_line: HR offers you more cover than you think you need.
D09.concept_body: A hospital bill arrives without warning and does not care what you have saved. Cover is cheap when you do not need it, and unavailable the moment you do.

D09-A.immediate_text: 5,400 a year for 5 lakhs of cover you hope to never use.
D09-A.deferred_text: Dengue, four days admitted, 1.1 lakh bill. Covered, with room to spare.

D09-B.option_label: Skip it, you are covered enough
D09-B.immediate_text: 450 a month saved. 3 lakhs is probably fine.
D09-B.deferred_text: Dengue, four days admitted, 1.1 lakh bill. Covered, but your cover for the year is gone.

D09-C.option_label: Skip cover, rely on the company policy
D09-C.immediate_text: Nothing leaves your account. The company policy covers 3 lakhs.
D09-C.deferred_text: You change jobs. The cover ends the day you leave.

D10.situation_text: Your closest school friend is getting married in Udaipur. Flights, hotel, clothes, gift: about 60,000. Six people from your group are going.
D10.why_it_matters: The Life bar exists so that saying no is not automatically the right answer.
D10.hook_line: Your closest school friend is getting married in Udaipur.

D10-A.immediate_text: Four days you will talk about for a decade. Savings back to near zero.
D10-A.deferred_text: The photos are still your phone wallpaper.

D10-B.option_label: Go, but train and shared room
D10-B.immediate_text: Same wedding, one third the cost, slightly worse sleep.
D10-B.deferred_text: Nobody remembers how you got there.

D10-C.immediate_text: You save 55,000 and watch it on your phone.
D10-C.deferred_text: The group photos are up. You are not in a single one.

D11.situation_text: Cracked screen, battery dead by 4pm. Repair is 3,000. A decent replacement is 18,000. The one you want is 73,000, or 6,600 a month for twelve months on no-cost EMI.
D11.why_it_matters: No-cost EMI is the gateway product. It teaches you that you can afford the monthly, not the thing.
D11.concept_body: There is no such thing. The cost is the cash discount you gave up. The same phone is cheaper if you pay for it outright, and the difference is the interest nobody called interest.

D11-A.deferred_text: Ten months on. It still works. The crack has spread across the top third.

D11-B.deferred_text: Eight months on. It does everything the 73,000 one does, a little slower.

D11-C.option_label: 6,600 a month for twelve months, no-cost EMI
D11-C.immediate_text: Best phone in the office. 6,600 committed every month for a year.
D11-C.deferred_text: Final EMI paid. The phone is a year old and the new model is out.

D12.situation_text: Your sister wants a coaching class. It costs 8,000. She has not asked your parents. She asked you.
D12.why_it_matters: The first time you become a source of money rather than a recipient.
D12.hook_line: Your sister asks you for something before she asks your parents.

D12-A.immediate_text: She is thrilled. She asks you not to tell your parents.
D12-A.deferred_text: She asks again, for something else. You are the default now.

D12-B.option_label: Pay half, ask her to tell your parents
D12-B.immediate_text: Slightly awkward. Handled in the open.
D12-B.deferred_text: Your parents cover the rest without being asked twice.

D12-C.option_label: Tell her to ask your parents
D12-C.immediate_text: She does. It takes two weeks and a fight.
D12-C.deferred_text: She got the class. She did not come to you again.

D13.situation_text: First appraisal: 8%. Inflation this year was about 6%. Your manager says the budget is fixed.
D13.why_it_matters: A raise below inflation is a pay cut. Almost nobody does this subtraction.
D13.concept_body: A raise below inflation is a pay cut. The number on the letter went up. What it buys went down. Only one of those is the raise.

D13-A.deferred_text: Two appraisals in, your buying power is almost exactly where it started.

D13-B.deferred_text: He remembers you asked. It comes up at the next cycle, both ways.

D13-C.immediate_text: Nothing changes this month. Your CV is updated.
D13-C.deferred_text: Two interviews reach final rounds around month 20.

D14.situation_text: Your bonus lands. 1.2 lakhs. At dinner your father mentions your cousin missed her coaching fee deadline. He does not ask you for anything.
D14.why_it_matters: The hardest money decisions in India are not asked out loud. They are mentioned.
D14.hook_line: A bonus lands. The largest amount you have ever held.
D14.concept_body: A bonus feels like extra, so it gets treated like extra. It is the only money you will ever receive that you have not already planned around, which is exactly why it disappears.

D14-A.option_label: Give her the full coaching fee, 80,000
D14-A.immediate_text: Your father does not say thank you. He tells his brother.
D14-A.deferred_text: She cleared the entrance. The 80,000 is not mentioned again.

D14-B.immediate_text: Your father covers the rest quietly. Nobody discusses it.
D14-B.deferred_text: She cleared it. The money you kept is still invested.

D14-C.immediate_text: Nothing is said. The subject does not come up again.
D14-C.deferred_text: She did not get the seat. It is never linked to you out loud.

D14-D.option_label: Spend a third on a trip, invest the rest
D14-D.immediate_text: The trip is the best week of the year so far.
D14-D.deferred_text: The photos are still on your phone. So is the family dinner where nobody spoke.

D15.situation_text: Your mother wants to put 60,000 of your money into gold. She calls it security. She means your wedding, though nobody says that.
D15.why_it_matters: Gold in an Indian family is not an asset decision. It is a relationship decision wearing an asset costume.

D15-A.immediate_text: She is happier than you expected. It goes in the locker the same week.
D15-A.deferred_text: {gold_change_pct}. You cannot sell it without a conversation.

D15-B.option_label: Put 20,000 in gold, invest the rest
D15-B.immediate_text: A compromise nobody is thrilled by. She accepts it.
D15-B.deferred_text: Small, steady, forgettable. You have not checked it since month 11.

D15-C.immediate_text: You explain compounding. She stops listening halfway.
D15-C.deferred_text: Gold had a good year. You hear the number at Diwali, twice.

D16.situation_text: You can start investing monthly. 5,000 into a broad equity index, 5,000 into a recurring deposit, or wait until you earn more.
D16.why_it_matters: This is the decision the whole product exists to rehearse. Time in the market beats amount invested at this age.
D16.hook_line: You have enough spare to start investing, if you want to.
D16.concept_body: A fixed amount invested every month, whatever the market is doing. Starting early matters more than starting big: the years do more work than the rupees.

D16-A.option_label: 5,000 a month into a broad equity index
D16-A.immediate_text: First investment. A month later it is {equity_change_pct}.
D16-A.deferred_text: Fourteen months. {equity_down_months} of them were red. The balance is {equity_balance} on {equity_contributed} put in.

D16-B.option_label: 5,000 a month into a recurring deposit
D16-B.immediate_text: Safe, predictable, about 6.5% a year before tax.
D16-B.deferred_text: It grew exactly as promised. Inflation took most of it.

D16-C.deferred_text: A year gone. You are still waiting to earn more.

D17.situation_text: Pre-approved credit card. 2 lakh limit, no annual fee. You did not apply for it.
D17.why_it_matters: The card is not the problem. The minimum payment button is the problem.
D17.hook_line: A credit card you did not apply for.
D17.concept_body: A record of whether you pay on time. Paying the full bill builds it. Paying the minimum quietly costs about 3.5% a month on everything left over.

D17-A.option_label: Take it, use it, pay in full every month
D17-A.immediate_text: Points, convenience, and a bill you clear on the due date.
D17-A.deferred_text: You have a credit history now, and it is good.

D17-B.option_label: Take it and leave it in a drawer
D17-B.immediate_text: No risk, no benefit, no history being built.
D17-B.deferred_text: The card was closed for non-use.

D17-C.option_label: Take it and pay the minimum when tight
D17-C.immediate_text: Suddenly you can afford things. The minimum is only 5%.
D17-C.deferred_text: Interest runs near 3.5% a month. The balance has barely moved in six months.

D17-D.deferred_text: You apply for something later with no credit history at all.

D18.situation_text: March. Payroll says you will lose 46,000 to tax unless you show investments. You have three weeks.
D18.why_it_matters: Panic tax saving in March is how people end up in twenty year products they did not want.
D18.hook_line: March, and payroll wants to know what you invested.
D18.concept_body: Some investments reduce the tax you pay, under section 80C. The old regime rewards them. The new one has lower rates and no deductions. Choosing in March, in a panic, is how people end up in products they did not want.

D18-A.immediate_text: Tax saved. You are now in a product you cannot exit for five years.
D18-A.deferred_text: You are still paying into something you did not choose.

D18-B.option_label: Compare the old and new regime first
D18-B.immediate_text: Two evenings of reading. The new regime is better for you this year.
D18-B.deferred_text: You redo the comparison in March without panicking.

D18-C.deferred_text: No regret, no product you resent. Also no saving.

D19.situation_text: The roof at home needs work before the monsoon. The quote is 1.4 lakhs. Your parents have told you about it twice and asked for nothing.
D19.why_it_matters: Most people meet their first large family obligation with no plan and no framework for saying a partial yes.

D19-A.immediate_text: It clears most of what you have saved in 13 months.
D19-A.deferred_text: The roof is done. Your father tells the story to visitors. Your savings restarted from zero.

D19-B.option_label: Send 50,000 and tell them that is what you have
D19-B.immediate_text: They accept it without comment. Your father arranges the rest himself.
D19-B.deferred_text: The roof is half done. It holds. Nobody mentions the other half.

D19-C.immediate_text: Your mother says it is fine. Your father changes the subject.
D19-C.deferred_text: They took a loan against the house. You found out from your aunt.

D20.situation_text: A colleague says he made 40% last year in small companies. He shows you the screen. Your index investment is {equity_change_pct}.
D20.why_it_matters: Nobody tells you about the year they lost 40%. The comparison is always against someone's best story.
D20.hook_line: A colleague shows you what he made last year.
D20.concept_body: You hear about the year someone made 40%. You do not hear about the year they lost it, or about everyone who did the same thing and quietly stopped mentioning it.

D20-A.immediate_text: Feels smart. First month it is {equity_change_pct}.
D20-A.deferred_text: That colleague has stopped mentioning it. Your balance is {equity_change_pct}.

D20-B.option_label: Keep the index, add small extra there
D20-B.immediate_text: A contained bet. You check it daily now.

D20-C.immediate_text: Nothing happens. He brings it up again at lunch, twice, in front of others.
D20-C.deferred_text: He has stopped mentioning it. So has everyone else at lunch.

D20-D.option_label: Start with 30,000 in small caps, like him
D20-D.immediate_text: Feels smart. You check the app before breakfast.
D20-D.deferred_text: {equity_change_pct}. You started with 30,000, at the top.

D21.situation_text: An agent offers 1 crore of term cover for about 800 a month at your age. You have no spouse, no children, no loan.
D21.why_it_matters: Term premium is locked at the age you buy. Waiting until you need it is the expensive path.
D21.hook_line: An agent wants to sell you something you do not need yet.
D21.concept_body: Pure cover, no returns, and the cheapest kind. The price is locked at the age you buy it. Waiting until you need it is the expensive way round.

D21-A.option_label: Buy the cover now, 800 a month
D21-A.immediate_text: 1 crore of cover. It feels pointless. That is why it is cheap.
D21-A.deferred_text: A colleague buys the same cover at 33 and pays more than double.

D21-B.option_label: Wait until you have people depending on you
D21-B.immediate_text: 800 a month saved. Nothing to protect yet.
D21-B.deferred_text: You look again later. The price has moved with your age, and so has your health.

D21-C.option_label: Take the plan that returns your premium
D21-C.immediate_text: Cover plus your money back at the end. Three times the price.
D21-C.deferred_text: You work out what the returned premium is actually worth after 30 years of inflation.

D22.situation_text: You are tired of autos. A scooter is 95,000, or 8,600 a month for a year at zero cost EMI. Your emergency fund is 32,000.
D22.why_it_matters: The emergency fund only works if it is boring and untouched.
D22.concept_body: Some things you buy lose value the moment you own them. A vehicle is worth less every month you keep it. That is not a mistake, but it is not saving either.

D22-A.immediate_text: Keys the same day. 8,600 committed for twelve months.
D22-A.deferred_text: The layoff lands while the EMI still has six months to run.

D22-B.option_label: Pay cash from the emergency fund
D22-B.immediate_text: Owned outright. Emergency fund is now almost nothing.
D22-B.deferred_text: The layoff lands. You have a scooter and no runway.

D22-C.deferred_text: No asset, no EMI. In month 22 only one of those matters.

D23.situation_text: Your father's business loan has 14,000 a month left to run for two years. He has not asked you. Your mother has.
D23.why_it_matters: A committed rupee is not the same as a spent rupee. This is what the Freedom bar measures.
D23.hook_line: Your mother calls about your father's loan.
D23.concept_body: Money that is already spoken for before it arrives. A large salary with large commitments buys fewer choices than a small one with none. This is what the Freedom bar counts.

D23-A.immediate_text: Your father does not say much. Your mother says a lot.
D23-A.deferred_text: Two years committed. Every other decision now bends around this.

D23-B.immediate_text: Shared load. The conversation stays open.
D23-B.deferred_text: Manageable. It still shows up in every month's maths.

D23-C.option_label: Say you cannot manage it right now
D23-C.immediate_text: True, and it does not feel true when you say it.
D23-C.deferred_text: They managed. Something changed in how they talk to you about money.

D24.situation_text: Landlord wants 4,000 more. A similar place 40 minutes further out saves you 5,000. Moving costs about 15,000.
D24.why_it_matters: Rent saved and time lost are both real. The game should not pretend one is free.
D24.concept_body: A cheaper rent forty minutes further out costs you eighty minutes a day. Whether that is a saving depends on what the time was worth, and nobody puts that on the lease.

D24-A.deferred_text: Six months of the longer commute. You have finished four books and you are never home before nine.

D24-B.immediate_text: 5,000 a month saved. Eighty minutes a day spent.
D24-B.deferred_text: The savings are real. So is how tired you are.

D24-C.immediate_text: He settles at 2,000 after you mention moving.
D24-C.deferred_text: You now know the rent was always negotiable.

D25.situation_text: Four weddings in six weeks. Travel, clothes and gifts come to about 45,000. Attend all, pick two, or send gifts only.
D25.why_it_matters: Wedding season is a predictable annual cost that nobody budgets for.

D25-A.immediate_text: Six weeks of travel. Your savings take the hit.
D25-A.deferred_text: Everyone was at every wedding. Nobody counted who spent what.

D25-B.option_label: Pick the two closest to you
D25-B.immediate_text: Two you actually cared about. Two polite apologies.

D25-C.option_label: Send gifts to all four, attend none
D25-C.deferred_text: Two of them have stopped calling.

D26.situation_text: Two offers. A large company at 9.5 LPA, stable. A six person startup at 7.3 LPA plus equity you cannot value.
D26.why_it_matters: Chapter defining fork. Sets how hard the month 22 layoff lands.
D26.hook_line: Two offers, and the job you already have.
D26.concept_body: Every choice is also the choices you did not make. The safe offer costs you the risky one's upside. The risky one costs you the safe one's certainty.

D26-A.immediate_text: Take home jumps by about 18,000. Predictable.
D26-A.deferred_text: A restructure hits your team anyway. Nobody is safe, only slower to fall.

D26-B.immediate_text: Small raise, real ownership, no idea what the equity is worth.
D26-B.deferred_text: Funding does not close. The layoff in month 22 is this decision arriving.

D27.situation_text: Your income went up. Your investing did not. Upgrade the flat, raise the SIP by the full increase, or split it.
D27.why_it_matters: Lifestyle creep is not one decision. It is the absence of one.
D27.hook_line: Your income went up. Your investing did not.
D27.concept_body: Spending rises to meet income without anyone deciding it should. It is not one purchase. It is the absence of a decision when the raise arrives.

D27-A.immediate_text: Better building, gym downstairs. The raise is already spoken for.
D27-A.deferred_text: The raise is gone and you would not notice if it were reversed.

D27-B.option_label: Put the entire increase into investing
D27-B.immediate_text: Your life looks identical. Your investment does not.
D27-B.deferred_text: Your monthly investing has doubled and your costs have not moved.

D27-C.immediate_text: A little more comfort, a little more invested.
D27-C.deferred_text: Costs flat, investing up. Month 22 is four months away.

D28.situation_text: Friday, 3pm. Role eliminated. One month severance. Your monthly costs are {monthly_costs}. You have whatever you have.
D28.why_it_matters: This is where every earlier Safety decision gets its receipt. The event is not optional, the response is.
D28.concept_body: How many months you survive with no income. Not a number most people know about themselves, and the only number that matters on the day the job goes.

D28-A.option_label: Cut everything, live off the emergency fund
D28-A.immediate_text: Costs down to 22,000. You calculate your runway daily.
D28-A.deferred_text: Six weeks of runway left. The number has not gone up.

D28-B.immediate_text: {stopped_monthly} a month back. The habit breaks in week one.
D28-B.deferred_text: You restarted four months later. Those months never come back.

D28-C.option_label: Put the gap on the credit card
D28-C.immediate_text: Nothing changes day to day. The balance grows quietly.
D28-C.deferred_text: You have a job again. The card balance is still there, and the minimum barely touches it.

D28-D.option_label: Ask your parents to cover you
D28-D.immediate_text: They say yes immediately. You hate it.
D28-D.deferred_text: Handled. It is mentioned at every family gathering for two years.

D29.situation_text: Two months without income. One offer at 6.3 LPA, below what you made. Another process reaches final round in three weeks.
D29.why_it_matters: Runway is what buys you the right to say no. Players feel this only after D28.
D29.hook_line: Two months without income, and one offer on the table.

D29-A.immediate_text: Income restarts at a lower number. The bleeding stops.
D29-A.deferred_text: Safe, smaller, and it took three years to get back to where you were.

D29-B.option_label: Wait three weeks for the better process
D29-B.immediate_text: No income, no certainty, one more month of runway gone.
D29-B.deferred_text: It came through at 10.5 LPA. The three weeks had no income at all.

D29-C.immediate_text: Irregular money, long days, no benefits.
D29-C.deferred_text: You kept the runway alive and took the better offer anyway.

D30.situation_text: A cousin is putting money into a scheme paying 3% a month, guaranteed. He has been paid on time for eight months. He wants you in.
D30.why_it_matters: Chapter closer. If a return is guaranteed and high, you are the return.
D30.hook_line: Your cousin has been paid on time for eight months.
D30.concept_body: A return that is both high and guaranteed does not exist. Someone is paying it out of something. Usually the next person's money, and usually not for long.

D30-A.immediate_text: Three months of payments arrive exactly on time.
D30-A.deferred_text: The payments stop. So does the cousin's phone.

D30-B.option_label: Put in 5,000 just to test it
D30-B.immediate_text: Small amounts come back on schedule. You consider adding more.
D30-B.deferred_text: The scheme collapses. The 5,000 does not come back.

D30-C.option_label: Stay out, and warn your parents
D30-C.immediate_text: Your cousin tells the family you called him a fraud. Your father almost invests anyway.
D30-C.deferred_text: It collapses. Your cousin has not spoken to you since Diwali.
